root_cause.text: The rxrpc_server_keyring() function lacks a check for whether rx->securities is already initialized, allowing multiple calls to overwrite the pointer and leak the reference count of the previously assigned keyring object.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds an early return check `if (rx->securities) return -EINVAL;` at the beginning of rxrpc_server_keyring(), preventing reassignment of rx->securities when it is already set. Without this check, a second call to rxrpc_server_keyring() would overwrite the existing rx->securities pointer with a new keyring reference without releasing the old one, causing the reference count of the original keyring to never be decremented and creating a memory leak.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The `rxrpc_server_keyring()` function fails to check if `rx->securities` is already set before assigning a new keyring, allowing multiple assignments that leak the reference count of previously assigned keyrings.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds an early check `if (rx->securities) return -EINVAL;` at the beginning of the function (lines 128-129). This prevents reassignment of the securities field when it is already populated. Without this check, the function would overwrite the existing `rx->securities` pointer without releasing its reference, causing a reference count leak on the previous keyring object. The fix ensures that `rx->securities` can only be set once per socket, preventing the leak that occurs when the field is reassigned multiple times.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add validation to prevent re-initialization of server keyring when security context already exists on the socket.
intent_record.what: Added a guard clause that checks if `rx->securities` is already set and returns -EINVAL if true, positioned before the existing optlen validation.
intent_record.how: This prevents the rxrpc_server_keyring function from proceeding if a security context has already been established on the socket. It enforces a constraint that the keyring can only be set once per socket, rejecting any subsequent attempts with an error code.
